dedupe_keys.name: portugal effect of heatwaves on daily hospital admissions by county 2000 to 2018

description: This case study quantifies how heatwaves increase daily hospital admissions across Portugal, where the effects of heat on morbidity, not mortality, had been little quantified. The authors, from Portuguese universities and health institutes, published it as an open-access journal article. They related daily hospital admissions at county level from 2000 to 2018 to heatwave days defined with the excess heat factor index, covering all major diagnostic categories, 25 disease categories and all age groups, over multiple heatwave events. Coverage is the whole of mainland Portugal. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives licence. Caveats: admission records are not released with the article, the heatwave index is one of several possible definitions, and associations are observational. The study found a statistically significant overall increase in daily admissions on heatwave days, an incidence rate ratio of 1.189, across all age groups and major causes, and presents itself as the first to estimate the full extent of heatwave effects on hospitalisations over 19 years for a whole country. Simulation uses: estimating heat-driven surges in hospital demand for capacity planning and climate adaptation of health services. Related records: the England heat admissions study (case_study-england-extreme-heat-hospital-admissions) and the Swiss heat admission costs study (case_study-switzerland-heat-hospital-admission-costs) give comparable estimates.
